mainTopic: The laws of עיבור שנה, and great חכמים who took blame on themselves to spare others shame
overview: This amud is about עיבור שנה, adding a month to make a leap year. It opens with the rule that only people the נשיא invited may join in the decision. A story shows the rule in action: רבן גמליאל found an uninvited eighth person, and שמואל הקטן said he was the one. The גמרא reveals that it was really someone else, and שמואל הקטן took the blame to save that person from shame. The גמרא then gives similar stories about רבי חייא and רבי מאיר, and traces this trait back through שמואל הקטן and שכניה בן יחיאל to how הקב"ה dealt with יהושע and משה. Next comes a ברייתא praising הלל הזקן and שמואל הקטן as worthy of the שכינה, along with שמואל הקטן's dying prophecy. The גמרא then returns to the laws: the נשיא must agree to a leap year, and only real needs like roads, bridges, ovens for the קרבן פסח, and travelers already on the way justify it. Young animals and birds may only serve as extra support, as in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's letter, and רב פפא explains that the court may add either twenty-nine or thirty days.

steps.title: Only invited people may add a leap month
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the ברייתא: עיבור שנה is done only by those invited for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The year is made a leap year only] by those who were invited for it.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a ruling that began just before this section. The ruling says a year can only be made a leap year by people specially invited to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a month to the year is not open to any qualified חכם who walks in. The נשיא picks the group, and only that chosen group may make the decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.english: by those who were invited for it.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started right before: 'A year is made a leap year only...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only those invited for the purpose may take part in עיבור שנה.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל finds an extra person in the loft
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל invited seven, found eight, and demanded that the uninvited one leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with רבן גמליאל, who said: Bring me seven people early to the upper room. He came early and found eight. He said: Who came up without permission? Let him go down!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story that shows the rule in action. רבן גמליאל wanted exactly the seven he invited, so he told the extra person to leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story proves the rule is serious. Even one uninvited person was not allowed to stay for the decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper room / loft where they met

phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said:
Bring me seven early to the upper room.
He came early and found eight.
He said: Who is it that came up
without permission? Let him go down!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that illustrates the rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only invited people may take part in עיבור שנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן גמליאל and the eight people in the loft.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן admits, and רבן גמליאל repeats the rule
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן says he came only to learn. רבן גמליאל praises him but restates that only invited people may decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל הקטן stood up and said: I am the one who came up without permission. I did not come to vote on the leap year. I needed to learn how the הלכה is done in practice. He said to him: Sit, my son, sit. All the years would deserve to be made leap years through you, but the חכמים said: The year is made a leap year only by those invited for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. שמואל הקטן takes responsibility, and רבן גמליאל honors him while still saying the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל makes clear that the problem was never whether the person was worthy. Even someone fully worthy cannot join the decision unless invited. That is why the rule is quoted again at the end of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: How the law is actually carried out

phrases.english: Shmuel HaKatan stood up and said:
I am the one who came up without permission,
and I did not come up to make the year a leap year,
but I needed to learn the practical halacha.
He said to him: Sit, my son, sit.
All of the years are worthy
to be made leap years through you,
but the Sages said:
The year is not made a leap year
except by those invited for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and states the rule outright.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל's own words: 'אמרו חכמים אין מעברין את השנה אלא במזומנין לה'.
steps.whatToRemember: Being worthy is not enough. For עיבור שנה you must also be invited.

steps.title: It wasn't really שמואל הקטן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reveals that someone else came uninvited. שמואל הקטן took the blame to spare him shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not really שמואל הקטן, but a different person. He did it because of the embarrassment [of that other person].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a surprising fact about the story. שמואל הקטן was innocent and only claimed guilt to protect the real person from embarrassment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This changes how we read the story. The 'I came to learn' line was not his real reason for being there. It was a kind cover-up. Now the story also teaches a lesson about protecting other people's dignity.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל הקטן is not the one who broke the rule. He only said he was, so the real person would not be shamed.

phrases.english: And it was not Shmuel HaKatan,
but another person,
and it was because of embarrassment that he did it.
phrases.notes: He means the other man's embarrassment. שמואל הקטן was covering for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets who actually came uninvited in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל הקטן took the blame on himself to save another person from shame.

steps.title: רבי חייא leaves רבי's lecture over garlic
steps.stepSummary: רבי smelled garlic and asked whoever ate it to leave. רבי חייא left, and then everyone left.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like when רבי was sitting and teaching and smelled garlic. He said: Whoever ate garlic should leave. רבי חייא stood up and left. Then everyone stood up and left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar story to show this kind of behavior. רבי חייא got up first, which made it easy for everyone to leave so no one was singled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a great person like רבי חייא walked out, everyone followed. So the person who really ate garlic could leave without anyone knowing it was him.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי וְקָא דָרֵישׁ,
phrases.english: Like that time when Rebbi was sitting and teaching,
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and he smelled the smell of garlic.
He said: Whoever ate garlic should leave.
Rabbi Chiya stood up and left.
Everyone stood up and left.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּיָתֵיב רַבִּי וְקָא דָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to שמואל הקטן's behavior.
steps.raayaObject: Taking blame on oneself to spare someone else shame.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי חייא and the garlic.

steps.title: רבי חייא reveals he did not eat garlic
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ברבי asks רבי חייא if he upset his father. רבי חייא answers that he would never do such a thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the morning, רבי שמעון the son of רבי found רבי חייא. He said to him: Are you the one who upset my father? He answered: Such a thing should not happen in Israel!
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by showing that רבי חייא was innocent. He left only to cover for whoever really ate the garlic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's strong denial shows he would never come to a lecture smelling of garlic. So his leaving was the same kind of cover-up that שמואל הקטן did.

keyTerms.meaning: Such a thing should not happen among Jews

phrases.english: In the morning Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi found him,
Rabbi Chiya.
He said to him: Are you the one
who upset my father?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא תְּהֵא כְּזֹאת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל!
phrases.english: He said to him: Such a thing should not be in Israel!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשַּׁחַר מְצָאוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reveals the truth behind רבי חייא's leaving.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי חייא was innocent. He took the blame to protect someone else, just like שמואל הקטן.

steps.title: Where did רבי חייא learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי חייא learned to take blame in order to protect others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did רבי חייא learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. It wants to know the source of רבי חייא's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Claiming guilt you don't have could seem wrong. So the גמרא looks for an earlier great person who acted this way, as a model.

keyTerms.meaning: From where did he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya, from where did he learn this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the behavior just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The earlier model for taking blame to spare someone else shame.

steps.title: From רבי מאיר, who wrote a גט for a woman
steps.stepSummary: A woman said one of רבי מאיר's students had married her through relations. רבי מאיר wrote her a גט, and everyone else did the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: From רבי מאיר, as a ברייתא teaches: A woman came to רבי מאיר's study hall. She said to him: רבי, one of you married me through relations. רבי מאיר stood up, wrote her a גט, and gave it to her. Then everyone stood up, wrote her a גט, and gave it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא learned this from רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר gave a גט first, so the real husband could also give one without being exposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since everyone gave a גט, the real man's גט freed her to remarry, and no one knew who he was. רבי מאיר acted as if he might be guilty to protect the guilty man's dignity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is one link in a chain of sources for taking blame on oneself to save another Jew from public shame. The גמרא goes on to trace it further back, to שמואל הקטן, שכניה בן יחיאל, and finally יהושע or משה.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל הקטן, רבי חייא, and רבי מאיר all made themselves look guilty to protect someone else from embarrassment.

phrases.english: From Rabbi Meir, as it was taught:
There was an incident with a certain woman

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּאתָה לְבֵית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: who came to the study hall of Rabbi Meir.
She said to him: My teacher,
one of you betrothed me through relations.
Rabbi Meir stood up and wrote her
a bill of divorce and gave it to her.
Everyone stood up, wrote, and gave her one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by citing a ברייתא about רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא learned it from רבי מאיר, who gave a גט first so the guilty man could give one too without being exposed.

steps.title: Where did רבי מאיר learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי מאיר learned to take blame on himself to protect others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did רבי מאיר learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps climbing backward up the chain. It asks who taught רבי מאיר this way of acting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רבי מאיר wrote a גט so the real student would not be shamed. Now the גמרא wants his source too, which sets up a whole chain of teachers.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, from where did he learn it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the habit of taking the blame so someone else won't be embarrassed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי מאיר's behavior described in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who רבי מאיר learned this behavior from.

steps.title: He learned it from שמואל הקטן
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learned it from שמואל הקטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: From שמואל הקטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר learned it from שמואל הקטן, whose story we saw in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל הקטן claimed he came uninvited so the real person would not be embarrassed. That earlier story becomes the model for רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: From Shmuel HaKatan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל הקטן was רבי מאיר's model.

steps.title: Where did שמואל הקטן learn it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שמואל הקטן's behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did שמואל הקטן learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one more step back. It asks who שמואל הקטן learned this from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same question repeats on purpose. The גמרא is building a chain to show this trait goes all the way back to תנ"ך.

phrases.english: And Shmuel HaKatan, from where did he learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain upward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of שמואל הקטן's behavior.

steps.title: He learned it from שכניה בן יחיאל
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הקטן learned it from שכניה בן יחיאל, who told עזרא "we sinned" by marrying foreign women.
steps.simpleTranslation: From שכניה בן יחיאל, as the פסוק says: שכניה told עזרא, "We broke faith with our God and married foreign women, yet there is still hope for Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק in which שכניה בן יחיאל says "we" sinned along with the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The common explanation is that שכניה himself is not listed later among the men who married foreign wives. He still said "we" so the guilty ones would not be singled out and shamed. That is the same move שמואל הקטן made.

keyTerms.meaning: A man in the time of עזרא

phrases.english: From Shecaniah ben Jehiel, as it is written:
"And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered
and said to Ezra: We have broken faith with our God
and have married foreign women of the peoples of the land

phrases.aramaic: וְעַתָּה יֵשׁ מִקְוֶה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל זֹאת״.
phrases.english: yet now there is hope for Israel concerning this."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שכניה בן יחיאל included himself among the sinners to protect them.

steps.title: Where did שכניה learn it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where שכניה בן יחיאל learned this trait.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did שכניה בן יחיאל learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The chain climbs once more. Now the גמרא asks who שכניה learned from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will come from the תורה and from נביאים, as if the trait were learned from הקב"ה Himself.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁכַנְיָה בֶן יְחִיאֵל מֵהֵיכָא גְּמַר לַהּ?
phrases.english: And Shecaniah ben Jehiel, from where did he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁכַנְיָה בֶן יְחִיאֵל מֵהֵיכָא גְּמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain upward.

steps.title: From יהושע: God would not name the sinner
steps.stepSummary: When יהושע asked who sinned, הקב"ה said "Am I an informer?" and told him to cast lots.
steps.simpleTranslation: From יהושע. הקב"ה said to him: "Get up, why are you falling on your face? Israel has sinned." יהושע asked, "Master of the world, who sinned?" He answered, "Am I an informer? Go cast lots."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that הקב"ה Himself refused to name the sinner directly. He told יהושע to find out through a גורל instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even הקב"ה did not want to point a finger at one person. He said "Israel has sinned" in general terms. This is the deepest root of protecting others from being exposed.

phrases.english: From Joshua, as it is written:
"And the Lord said to Joshua: Get yourself up

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה זֶּה אַתָּה נֹפֵל עַל פָּנֶיךָ
phrases.english: why do you fall upon your face?
Israel has sinned."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, מִי חָטָא?
phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe, who sinned?
He said to him: And am I an informer?
Go cast lots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב"ה refused to name the sinner to יהושע.

steps.title: Another option: from משה
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the source is משה: הקב"ה said "How long will you refuse," blaming everyone in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it comes from משה, as the פסוק says: "How long will you refuse?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible source. When a few people went out to collect מן on שבת, הקב"ה spoke to משה as if everyone were guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a few people sinned, but the פסוק says "you" in plural and speaks to משה. That way no one person is exposed. It teaches the same lesson as the יהושע story.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead

steps.whatToRemember: The chain: רבי חייא → רבי מאיר → שמואל הקטן → שכניה בן יחיאל → יהושע (or משה). Covering for someone to save them from shame is a trait that goes back to how הקב"ה acts.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: from Moses,
as it is written: "How long do you refuse."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second possible answer to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב"ה spoke to משה about all of Israel instead of naming the few who sinned.

steps.title: After the last נביאים, only a בת קול remained
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when חגי, זכריה and מלאכי died, רוח הקודש left Israel, but they still used a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: once the last prophets, חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, died, רוח הקודש left Israel. Even so, they still made use of a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא, brought because שמואל הקטן was just mentioned. This line sets the background for the stories that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real נבואה ended, but a lower level of message from שמים, a בת קול, still existed. The next stories describe what a בת קול said.

keyTerms.meaning: A heavenly voice, literally "daughter of a voice"

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Once the last prophets died,
Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi,
the Divine Spirit departed from Israel.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיוּ מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בְּבַת קוֹל.
phrases.english: But even so, they would make use of a Divine Voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא because שמואל הקטן was mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After נבואה ended, a בת קול was still in use.

steps.title: The בת קול in יריחו points to הלל הזקן
steps.stepSummary: In יריחו a בת קול said someone there was worthy of the שכינה like משה רבינו. The חכמים understood it meant הלל הזקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once, they were sitting in the upper room of the house of Gurya in יריחו. A בת קול came from שמים: "Someone here deserves to have the שכינה rest on him like משה רבינו, but his generation is not worthy." The חכמים looked to הלל הזקן. When he died, they mourned: "Alas, the pious one! Alas, the humble one! A student of עזרא!"
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first story in the ברייתא. It tells how הלל הזקן was recognized as worthy of נבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was not הלל himself. His generation was not worthy. This first story sets the pattern that the next story about שמואל הקטן will repeat.

phrases.english: One time they were reclining
in the upper room of the house of Gurya in Jericho,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִתְּנָה עֲלֵיהֶם בַּת קוֹל מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם:
phrases.english: and a Divine Voice was given to them from Heaven:
There is one here who is fit
for the Divine Presence to rest upon him like Moses our teacher,
but his generation is not deserving of it.

phrases.aramaic: נָתְנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת עֵינֵיהֶם בְּהִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן.
phrases.english: The Sages set their eyes on Hillel the Elder.
And when he died, they said about him:
Alas, the pious one; alas, the humble one,
phrases.notes: "הִי" is a cry of mourning, like "Oh, how we lost..."

phrases.english: a disciple of Ezra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first example of the בת קול described in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל הזקן was worthy of the שכינה, but his generation was not.

steps.title: The בת קול in יבנה points to שמואל הקטן
steps.stepSummary: In יבנה a בת קול again said someone was worthy of the שכינה. The חכמים understood it meant שמואל הקטן, a student of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, they were sitting in an upper room in יבנה. A בת קול came from שמים: "Someone here deserves to have the שכינה rest on him, but his generation is not worthy." The חכמים looked to שמואל הקטן. When he died, they mourned: "Alas, the pious one! Alas, the humble one! A student of הלל!"
steps.whatsHappening: This second story is the reason the ברייתא was brought. It shows how great שמואל הקטן was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story copies the הלל story almost word for word, with one difference. Here the words "like משה רבינו" are missing. שמואל הקטן is also called a student of הלל, which links him to the chain of humble, pious people.

keyTerms.meaning: יבנה, the town where the חכמים gathered after the בית שני

steps.confusionAlert: "Student of הלל" does not have to mean he studied with הלל in person. It can mean he followed in הלל's ways.

phrases.english: Another time they were reclining
in an upper room in Yavne,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִתְּנָה עֲלֵיהֶם בַּת קוֹל מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם:
phrases.english: and a Divine Voice was given to them from Heaven:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ כָּאן אֶחָד שֶׁרָאוּי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה עָלָיו שְׁכִינָה,
phrases.english: There is one here who is fit for the Divine Presence to rest upon him,
but his generation is not deserving of it.

phrases.aramaic: נָתְנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת עֵינֵיהֶם בִּשְׁמוּאֵל הַקָּטָן.
phrases.english: The Sages set their eyes on Shmuel HaKatan.
And when he died, they said about him:
Alas, the pious one; alas, the humble one,
a disciple of Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second story, now about שמואל הקטן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל הקטן was worthy of the שכינה, but his generation was not.

steps.title: שמואל הקטן's prophecy as he died
steps.stepSummary: As he was dying, שמואל הקטן foretold that שמעון and ישמעאל would be killed by the sword, their friends executed, the people plundered, and great troubles would come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also said when he was dying: "שמעון and ישמעאל to the sword, their friends to execution, the rest of the people to plunder, and many troubles will come upon the world."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by quoting the last words of שמואל הקטן. They were a prediction of terrible times ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows he truly had a touch of prophecy, matching the בת קול's praise. The שמעון and ישמעאל he named are usually understood as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל כהן גדול, who were killed by the Romans.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of his death

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל הקטן was humble enough to take the blame for others, and great enough to deserve the שכינה. In his last words he foretold the destruction that was coming.

phrases.english: He also said at the time of his death:
Shimon and Yishmael to the sword,
phrases.notes: These are generally understood as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and their companions to execution,
and the rest of the nation to plunder,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָקָן סַגִּיאָן עֲתִידָן לְמֵיתֵי עַל עָלְמָא.
phrases.english: and many troubles are destined to come upon the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds שמואל הקטן's dying words to his story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל הקטן foretold the killing of the leaders and coming troubles.

steps.title: No eulogy for יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים wanted to give יהודה בן בבא the same praise-eulogy, but could not, because he was killed by the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also wanted to say the same eulogy about יהודה בן בבא. But the moment was lost, because we do not eulogize people killed by the government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of the great people who were worthy of the שכינה. It adds that the חכמים wanted to praise יהודה בן בבא the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים eulogized שמואל הקטן with special words of praise. They wanted to say the same about יהודה בן בבא. Because the government killed him, a public eulogy was not possible, so the chance was lost.

keyTerms.meaning: the moment was lost (literally, 'the hour was torn')

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the section about the בת קול and the great people who were worthy of the שכינה.

phrases.english: And about Yehuda ben Bava
they wanted to say the same thing,
phrases.notes: He means the same eulogy said for שמואל הקטן: 'Alas, the pious one, alas, the humble one.'

phrases.english: but the moment was disrupted,
because we do not eulogize
those killed by the government.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא בִּקְּשׁוּ לוֹמַר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of שמואל הקטן's death and eulogy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People killed by the government are not eulogized, so יהודה בן בבא did not get the eulogy.

steps.title: The נשיא must agree to a leap year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a year is made a leap year only if the נשיא wants it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: We add a month to the year only if the נשיא wants it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, making a leap year. It quotes a ברייתא saying the נשיא must agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a leap year is not only a vote of the court. The leader of the סנהדרין, the נשיא, has to want it too. Without his agreement, the leap year does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: making the year a leap year by adding a month

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not add a month to the year
unless the Nasi wants it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יִרְצֶה נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the laws of the leap year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year needs the agreement of the נשיא.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל agrees after the fact
steps.stepSummary: While רבן גמליאל was away, the court made a leap year on condition that he would agree. When he returned and agreed, the leap year took effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once רבן גמליאל went to get permission from a governor in Syria and was delayed in returning. The court made the year a leap year on condition that רבן גמליאל would agree. When he came and said 'I agree,' the year turned out to be a leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story to show how the rule about the נשיא works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא was away, and the time to decide was running out. So the court made the leap year conditional on his agreement. His later 'I agree' made the leap year valid from the start. This shows that his agreement can come after the court's decision.

keyTerms.meaning: a governor or officer of the ruling government

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabban Gamliel
who went to get permission
from a certain governor in Syria,
and he was delayed in coming back,
and they made the year a leap year
on condition that Rabban Gamliel would agree.
And when Rabban Gamliel came
and said, "I agree,"
the year turned out to be a leap year.
phrases.notes: 'Turned out' means it counted as a leap year from the time the court decided.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁהָלַךְ לִיטּוֹל רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the rule about the נשיא through a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That the נשיא's agreement is needed, and that it can come afterward on condition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן גמליאל and the governor in Syria.

steps.title: Good reasons for a leap year
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא lists real needs that justify a leap year: roads, bridges, ovens for the קרבן פסח, and exiles already traveling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: We add a month only if it is needed: because of the roads, the bridges, the ovens for the קרבן פסח, or Jews from the exile who already left home and have not yet arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא listing which needs are good enough reasons to make a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reason concerns people being able to come to ירושלים and bring the קרבן פסח properly. Damaged roads or bridges, broken ovens for roasting, and travelers still on the road are all real obstacles. Adding a month gives time to fix these problems.

keyTerms.meaning: ovens for roasting the קרבן פסח

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not add a month to the year
unless it is needed,
because of the roads,
phrases.notes: He means roads damaged by rain, so people cannot travel to ירושלים for פסח.

phrases.english: and because of the bridges,
and because of the ovens for the Pesach offerings,
and because of the Jews of the exile
who have left their homes
and have not yet arrived.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה צְרִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who must agree to which reasons count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leap year is made for real needs: roads, bridges, Pesach ovens, and travelers already on the way.

steps.title: Reasons that do not count
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא says snow, cold, and exiles who have not yet set out are not reasons for a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But not because of snow, not because of cold, and not because of Jews of the exile who have not left their homes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the other side: things that are not good enough reasons for a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snow and cold make the trip unpleasant but do not stop it. People who have not even set out are treated differently from people already traveling. Only those already on the road get the extra time.
steps.confusionAlert: Both lists mention גָּלִיּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל. The difference is whether they already left home. Already traveling counts. Not yet left does not count.

phrases.english: But not because of the snow,
and not because of the cold,
and not because of the Jews of the exile
who have not left their homes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrast list to the valid reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Snow, cold, and exiles who have not set out do not justify a leap year.

steps.title: Young animals only support the decision
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא says young goats, lambs, and young birds are not reasons by themselves, but they can be added as supporting reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: We do not add a month because of the young goats, the lambs, or the young birds that cannot fly yet. But we use them as a support for adding to the year.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא lists reasons that cannot make a leap year on their own but can help support one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small animals and young birds would be better for קרבנות if there were more time. This alone is not enough to add a month. Once there is a real reason, though, these points can be added to strengthen the decision.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not add a month to the year
not because of the young goats,
and not because of the lambs,
and not because of young birds that cannot fly yet,
but we do make them
a support for adding to the year.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְעַבְּרִין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה לֹא מִפְּנֵי הַגְּדָיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third group: reasons that only support the decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young animals and birds are not a reason alone, but can support a leap year.

steps.title: How are they used as support?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how these animal reasons are used as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: what does it look like to use these reasons as support?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the animals are a 'support' but did not show what that means. This question asks for a concrete example.

phrases.english: How so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an example of the 'support' just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical example of using animals and birds as a supporting reason.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's leap-year letter. It mentions the young birds, thin lambs, and late spring as reasons for adding thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי says in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: 'We are letting you know that the young birds are tender, the lambs are thin, and the time of spring has not arrived. The matter seemed good to me, and I have added thirty days to this year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the actual words of a leap-year announcement that lists the animals as reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main reason is that spring has not come yet, and פסח must be in the spring. The tender birds and thin lambs are mentioned next to it as extra support. This is exactly what 'support' means: the animal reasons stand beside a real reason.
steps.whatToRemember: A leap year needs the נשיא's agreement and a real need. Young animals and birds only add support, as in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's announcement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says
in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
We are letting you know
that the young birds are tender,
and the lambs are thin,
and the time of spring has not arrived,
and the matter seemed good in my eyes,
and I have added onto this year
thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'how so' question with a real announcement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The announcement names the birds and lambs alongside the late spring as reasons for adding thirty days.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the added time is a regular month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the letter from a ברייתא. There the חכמים say the added month is thirty days, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is a regular month.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: How much is added in a leap year? Thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what it just quoted. In his letter רבן שמעון בן גמליאל added thirty days, but in this ברייתא he says only 'a month'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular month in the calendar is twenty-nine days. In the ברייתא, the 'thirty days' opinion belongs to the חכמים, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and says 'a month'. So his letter seems to go against his own opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year by adding time to it
Here: a regular month of twenty-nine days

steps.confusionAlert: 'Month' and 'thirty days' are not the same here. 'Month' means a regular twenty-nine-day month, so the two opinions really disagree.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
How much is the addition of a leap year?
Thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A month.
phrases.notes: He means a regular month, which is twenty-nine days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the thirty days mentioned in the letter quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The letter of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which adds thirty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the added time is a regular twenty-nine-day month. So how could his letter add thirty days?

steps.title: רב פפא: the court may choose either length
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the court may add either a regular month or thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If they want, a month; if they want, thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not mean that only a regular month is allowed. He meant the court has a choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים require thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל also allows a regular twenty-nine-day month. Since the court may also choose thirty days, his letter does not contradict his view in the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the court may add either twenty-nine or thirty days. So his thirty-day letter fits his own view.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If they want, a month,
if they want, thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: רָצוּ – חֹדֶשׁ, רָצוּ – שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the opinion: 'a month' gives a choice and does not require a regular month
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows only a twenty-nine-day month, so his letter contradicts him.
steps.terutzMaskana: He lets the court choose either a regular month or thirty days, so the letter fits his view.

steps.title: Opening a comparison about the letter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new comment about the letter. It says, 'Come and see the difference between' and the rest continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and see what difference there is between...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to compare two things related to the leap-year letter, and the comparison continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about thirty days is now settled. The phrase 'come and see' tells us the גמרא is opening a new observation, not continuing the argument about the calendar.

phrases.english: Come and see what difference there is between

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the length of the month, the גמרא turns back to the letter from step 27 to make a new observation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a comparison connected to the leap-year letter. The comparison is finished in the next section.
